CSCO.rationale: Cisco shows solid fundamental health with accelerating revenue and earnings growth (Q2 FY2026 revenue +9.7% YoY, EPS +31.1% YoY), strong gross margins (~65%), and a manageable balance sheet (debt-to-equity 0.52). The AI infrastructure opportunity is real with $1.9B in AI orders in Q3 and triple-digit hyperscaler growth. However, valuation has expanded dramatically — P/E has moved from ~28x a year ago to ~40.5x currently, near the top of its 365-day range (27-47x), while P/B has surged from ~6x to ~9.4x. This rich valuation largely prices in the AI-driven growth narrative. Key concerns include: (1) operating cash flow declined 43% QoQ and 19% YoY in the latest quarter, (2) security segment revenue declined 4% YoY per Q2 results, (3) RPO growth of 5% YoY lags revenue growth of 10%, suggesting the software transition is not keeping pace, and (4) gross margin slipped 260bps on higher memory costs. The upcoming Q4 FY2026 earnings on July 30 with guidance for $16.7-16.9B revenue and EPS of $1.16-1.18 could serve as a near-term catalyst, but the stock's +44.6% quarterly price surge already reflects much of this optimism. The ex-dividend date of July 6 is imminent but is a minor, well-known event. Net: good business trajectory but stretched valuation and some quality-of-earnings concerns cap the attractiveness.
